question: Do multiple-choice gains from context-augmented supervision transfer to open-ended exact match/F1 on the same questions, or does the multiple-choice format inflate the apparent effect?
description: The published context-over-KG advantage is measured only as four-way multiple-choice accuracy over generated options whose distractors come from the same KG/CG. Option selection can be easier than free-form answer generation: a model may benefit from context when discriminating among four candidates without being able to produce the answer entity string. Whether the same context effect survives under open-ended exact match/F1 on the same items is unmeasured, so the size (and possibly the sign) of the effect under the metric the refined question proposes is unknown.
rationale: If the effect is largely a discrimination effect, the practical claim and the comparison with generation-based KGQA systems weaken; the experiment is inexpensive to add (same checkpoints, re-scored with open-ended prompts) and directly affects how the refined contribution should be stated.
